method: Per-node: real MH/MW/PE/SIMD/weight_bits/act_bits/resType/ram_style fed into conv_cost_pe_simd() via a synthetic 1x1-kernel LayerGeometry (cin=MW,cout=MH) to isolate mvu_lut alone (no SWU/threshold bundled in)

new_value: Empirical joint threshold, not a regression: for ram_style="auto" MVAU_rtl/VVAU_hls nodes, checked whether real_BRAM18eq>0 as a function of wmem=(MW*MH)/(PE*SIMD) and mem_width=SIMD*weight_bits*PE. FINN's own bram_estimation() has no auto special-case at all to port (confirmed via local finn source checkout) -- Vivado's synthesis-time inference isn't exposed in FINN's Python code, so this had to be reverse-engineered from real per-node data instead of ported.
notes: Every one of the 10 real nonzero-BRAM rows has wmem>=256 AND mem_width>=16; all other 179 (up to wmem=288 at smaller mem_width) are exactly 0 -- zero counter-examples either direction in this sample. Implemented as a branch in conv_cost_pe_simd (RAM_STYLE_AUTO) plus a 3-way choice in layer_cost_pe_simd_auto_ram (block/auto/ultra, pick cheapest). ALSO found and fixed the actual bug: finn_milp.py's main per-layer loop was hard-coding RAM_STYLE_BLOCK for every MVAU/VVAU weight tile with a comment claiming that's "what real hardware does" -- false, per this same data (179/189 real auto-style nodes use LUTRAM, not block). Changed to RAM_STYLE_AUTO. Re-validated end-to-end against all 226 real MVAU/VVAU rows post-fix: aggregate real/raw ratio 0.028 -> 0.987, 179/181 zero-real rows now correctly predicted zero (was 0/181). Small sample right at the boundary (only 10 nonzero points) -- revisit with more data before trusting far above wmem~300.

notes: Per-build avg_bits means: v1=7.58, v2=4.53, v4=6.70, warmstart=5.64 -- the flat constant was only ever validated near warmstart's own mean, and was badly wrong at the other three (v1 +69.7%, v4 +72.4%, v2 -9.0% under the old flat rate). Per-build MVAU-only LUT error after refit: v1 +12.4%, v2 +10.9%, v4 +40.1%, warmstart -0.2% -- v4's residual is not fully closed by an avg_bits-linear term alone, some other confound remains unidentified. Full-network aggregate (all modelled node kinds, not MVAU-only) error narrows from a 22-point v2/v4 spread (+3.0%/+25.0%) to a 3-point spread (+13.5%/+16.2%) -- the real win here is turning a sign-flipping, unpredictable bias into a smaller, consistently-signed one. method: Decision-stump misclassification scan over PE*numSteps / NumChannels*numSteps / PE*NumChannels*numSteps (cutoff), then 1-term OLS through origin on the above-cutoff subset only (rate), via hardware/fit_threshold_bram_cutoff.py
notes: real PE degenerate at 1 in both builds (folding-config-propagation bug, see the threshold_lut rows above -- not yet deployed to a rebuild), so PE*numSteps collapses to numSteps-only, which does NOT separate zero/nonzero BRAM rows at all; NumChannels*numSteps won instead, but is still NOT a clean boundary -- 85/340 (25.0%) misclassified at the chosen cutoff, unlike mvau_weight_bram's zero-counterexample sample. Per-build aggregate threshold-BRAM error: v2 -26.7%->-29.2% (slightly worse), v4 +47.4%->+22.5% (nearly halved) -- net improvement in total absolute error, sign flip NOT closed. real_LUTRAM confirmed exactly 0 for all 340 rows (same as prior refits) -- ram_style capture (dump_node_attrs_all.py's ATTR_KEYS lacks the real depth_trigger_bram/depth_trigger_uram nodeattrs for Thresholding_rtl) would not have changed this fit; added for future builds only, see finn_cost_model.md.
